message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's morally acceptable for me to tell my cousin that his kid can't stay in our house. Let me break this down step by step. First, the situation: My cousin moved in with my husband and me. We converted a large main bedroom and bathroom into a separate flatlet for him, so it's like two separate units in one house. He has his own entrance, so there's no access from his part to ours. He doesn't have keys to come and go as he pleases. My cousin has a 2-year-old, and he's in the middle of a custody battle with his ex. He wants to spend more time with his son, and I support that. Yesterday, he asked if we could convert our spare bedroom into a room for his son when he comes over weekends. I understand that the court is looking into his living situation to see if he has suitable space for his son. His current room and bathroom are more than big enough, but I'm not comfortable letting his son sleep in our house because my cousin has no access to him. I don't want to take responsibility for his kid. The whole family is involved because that's just how my family is. Everyone expects me to help out my cousin with his custody situation to get him more time with his son. So, the question is: Would it be wrong (WIBTA) to tell my cousin I won't allow his son to stay in our house, potentially jeopardizing his court case? Hmm. Let me think about the moral aspects here. On one hand, I'm supporting my cousin in getting more time with his son, which is a good thing. I've already made space for him in our house, which shows I'm trying to help. But now he's asking to use our spare bedroom for his son, and I'm hesitant because I don't want to take responsibility for the child. I don't have access to his part of the house, and he doesn't have access to ours. So, if his son is in our house, I would be the one responsible for him. That's a big responsibility, especially for a 2-year-old. I don't feel comfortable with that. Also, the court is evaluating his living situation. If I say no, it might look like he doesn't have a suitable space, which could hurt his custody case. But I don't want to compromise my own comfort and safety by having his son in our house. Is it morally wrong to prioritize my own comfort over my cousin's custody case? Or is it acceptable because I'm not obligated to take on that responsibility? I think about the concept of autonomy. I have the right to decide what happens in my house. If I don't feel comfortable having his son there, I shouldn't be forced to. But then, there's the family expectation. Everyone expects me to help, which adds pressure. But does that mean I have a moral obligation to comply? I don't think so. My well-being and comfort are important too. Another angle: Is this action causing unnecessary harm? If I say no, it might negatively impact his custody case. But is that my responsibility? I'm not a legal expert, and I can't control the court's decision. I also consider the potential consequences. If his son can't stay with us, maybe he can find another arrangement. Or perhaps the court will understand that it's a separate living situation. In the end, I think it's morally acceptable to prioritize my own comfort and boundaries. I'm not obligated to take on the responsibility of his son, especially if it makes me uncomfortable. It's important to set limits, even when helping family.
